threads.body: Elasticsearch 7's `ActionType` is concrete and has a public name-taking constructor, so multiple actions with different wire names can have the exact same runtime class (including plugin actions). After the first `ActionType` is cached here, every later instance would report that first name for `db.operation.name` and the span name. Cache by action identity instead; `Cache.weak()` already uses identity comparison and the normally-singleton action lifetime keeps the cache bounded.

replies.body:
Addressed in d4f45e5fe86702ed9694ea8e834b2dbd7f89bfc8.

Analysis: The comment is correct. `ActionType` in Elasticsearch 7 is a concrete class with a public constructor accepting a name string. Two distinct `ActionType` instances can share the same runtime class while having different wire names. The original code keyed the cache on `Class<?>`, so the second instance would silently return the first instance's cached name. Switching to `Cache<Object, String>` keyed on the action instance itself uses `Cache.weak()`'s identity semantics and resolves the name once per distinct action object rather than once per class.

Upsides: Correctly reports `db.operation.name` for all `ActionType` instances including plugin actions with custom names. The cache remains bounded because action objects are effectively singletons in practice and the weak reference allows GC when they are not.

Downsides: No material downside identified. The change is strictly more correct and has the same asymptotic memory and performance characteristics.
